# fetch_species.py reads the pins from here and refuses to proceed on a mismatch, because a
# silently revised source would change what the database contains without changing any code.

column4: asked of the taxon, never of a particular host: the study exists to find UNREPORTED host associations
any species inside a qualifying genus that has an annotated assembly is in
oomycetes out since 2026-10-13

a LABEL, never a filter. The analysed cohort is field Triticum aestivum (1,450 runs); the 84 related-cereal runs in release/01_cohort are FIELD runs deposited inside cohort BioProjects and are the host contrast, not noise. Filtering the reference to fungi already recorded on wheat would make an unreported host association structurally undetectable, which is the finding this chapter exists to make. Recording which fungi ARE already known on wheat is what lets a detection be called novel
3 USDA records give the host as the common name 'wheat', all Puccinia from Wakefield & Hansford 1948-49 (Uganda). Aliased so they are not silently missed

names OF the taxon. `authority` carries the author string and `type material` is a strain designation; matching a bare binomial against either invites false positives. `includes` is accepted but flagged, being loose subsumption rather than equivalence

column3: PHI-base, experimental pathogenicity on a plant host
column4: FUNGuild and FungalTraits assign plant-pathogen at genus by name substring and inherit homonyms (37 of 39 db_v4 pathogen labels were genus priors on chytrids and industrial yeasts). PHI-base is curated per species from pathogenicity experiments and carries the NCBI taxid of both pathogen and host, so is_pathogen and is_wheat_pathogen are a join, not a guess. It is a LABEL, never scope: 0 PHI-base wheat pathogens fall outside the USDA master

column3: a cohort host that can hold its own k-mer space
column4: hosts are in the database as a SINK, not to be detected: without them a plant read is absorbed by the nearest fungal CDS and reported as a fungal hit. The host CALL is a second, separate use (04_assign ranks reads across hosts), and it is why an outgroup is carried
Triticum aestivum, the analysed host (1,450 cohort runs). Always in

a cohort host OUTSIDE the analysed genus is included when its genus holds at least this fraction of the cohort. Hordeum is 61/1,560 = 3.9% and is in; Triticosecale (0.6%) and Secale (0.3%) are not. Below this a host call is a curiosity, not a stratum the chapter reports

THE LOAD-BEARING EXCLUSION. T. turgidum, T. dicoccon and Triticum sp. are NOT added, because db_v3 held both hexaploid T. aestivum and tetraploid T. turgidum and 27.7% of the Triticum clade's 51.8M minimizers migrated to the genus node, so a correct wheat call scored low coverage. db_v4 fixed that by consolidating; re-adding them would re-create it. They call as T. aestivum, which is taxonomically honest

Arabidopsis thaliana, a DECLARED dicot outgroup, not derived from the cohort. Carried for mislabel QC only (~10M minimizers): host assignment RANKS rather than thresholds, so with only cohort hosts present every library is called as one of them and a contaminated or mislabelled library is undetectable. This is how Fragaria's absence was found, 30 strawberry runs landing on Populus, Arachis and Glycine
host CDS, NEVER host genomes. These are RNA-seq libraries so the transcriptome is what reads come from, and wheat CDS is ~0.2 GB against ~15 GB genomic

NOT NCBI. NCBI GenBank has the wheat pangenome as ASSEMBLIES and not as gene models: 8 of its 12 annotated T. aestivum entries carry protein_coding_gene_count = 0 (the NIAB cultivars), leaving only Chinese Spring annotated. Ensembl Plants has 19 T. aestivum cultivars WITH CDS, which is the breadth a sink wants

the analysed host takes EVERY cultivar Ensembl publishes, because that is where the reads are and a cultivar-specific transcript absent from the sink leaks onto a fungus. A contrast or outgroup host takes its REFERENCE only: barley is 57 runs and Arabidopsis is QC, so 77 barley cultivars would be weight without a question behind it

Ensembl files barley under 112509 (H. vulgare subsp. vulgare), not the cohort's 4513. CDS is tagged with the COHORT's species taxid so a host call resolves at the rank the cohort records and the chapter reports, the same reason 1047171 is used for Z. tritici rather than the IPO323 strain node 336722
the host CDS source, annotated pangenomes

PINNED, and pinnable in a way assembly_summary.txt is not: Ensembl publishes immutable numbered releases. NOTE THE TWO NUMBERING SYSTEMS: Ensembl Genomes numbers plants releases separately from Ensembl core, so this is EG plants release-63, which summary.txt describes as 'Release 116 of Ensembl plants' because it is loaded into Ensembl v116 databases. /pub/release-116/ does not exist. current/ was verified byte-identical to release-63/
the species table: name, taxonomy_id, assembly, assembly_accession
one directory per species, holding <Species>.<assembly>.cds.all.fa.gz
